$comment: Native toolchain versions. Single source of truth, read by flake.nix
(builtins.fromJSON), by the CI workflows, and by 'just doctor'.
JSON rather than EDN because nix can only parse JSON natively.
The FoundationDB client must match the server the testcontainers
image builds and the cluster the chart deploys, and protoc must
stay on the 25.x line because a newer protoc emits protobuf 4 code
that the FDB Record Layer's pinned protobuf-java 3.25.9 runtime
Changing a version means changing its sha256 in the same edit:
Cross-check against the vendor's published checksum where one exists;
FoundationDB publishes a .sha256 asset beside each package.
Copies that cannot read this file -- the Dockerfile ARG defaults and
the Helm values -- are asserted against it by scripts/check-versions.sh,
which runs in CI and as 'just check-versions'.

Keycloak is here for a different reason than the toolchain entries: the operator's CRD is generated from the server's realm schema, so an operator older than the server rejects fields the server exports. That surfaced as a restore failing with a strict decoding error on webAuthnPolicyResidentKey -- an hour into a teardown cycle, and only on the restore path, because the chart's committed realm JSON happens to carry no such field. Server and operator move together.

keycloak.$comment: Server image and operator image. The operator vendors its CRDs, so infra/helm/queenswood/charts/keycloak-operator must be re-vendored from keycloak-k8s-resources at this same tag when this changes.
